objects.description: This header defines no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. It only contains preprocessor macros for configuration (feature/test macros, package/version info, and header/function availability). There are no custom data types to extract.

Forward iterator over parallel arrays of enum integral values and their names. Useful for ranged-like iteration over enum metadata produced by Thrift. Equality treats any end position (index == n or n == -1) as equivalent. Stores raw pointers; lifetime of arrays must outlive the iterator.
Base exception type for Thrift C++. Carries an optional message and overrides std::exception::what(). Designed to be subclassed by specific Thrift exceptions.
Abstract interface for capturing an exception to be rethrown later (deferred throw). Provides a static templated factory and a pure virtual throw_it().

Concrete exception class for Apache Thrift application-level errors. Carries a message (via TException base) and a typed error code (TApplicationExceptionType). Provides serialization methods read/write using protocol::TProtocol and overrides what() to include a default message based on the type when no explicit message is set. Construction can specify type, message, or both. Lifetime and ownership are standard C++ object semantics; no special destruction required.

objects.definition:
enum TApplicationExceptionType {
    UNKNOWN = 0,
    UNKNOWN_METHOD = 1,
    INVALID_MESSAGE_TYPE = 2,
    WRONG_METHOD_NAME = 3,
    BAD_SEQUENCE_ID = 4,
    MISSING_RESULT = 5,
    INTERNAL_ERROR = 6,
    PROTOCOL_ERROR = 7,
    INVALID_TRANSFORM = 8,
    INVALID_PROTOCOL = 9,
    UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT_TYPE = 10
  };
objects.description: Scoped enum inside TApplicationException enumerating the category of application error. Values cover common Thrift RPC issues like wrong method, bad sequence id, missing result, protocol/transform issues, etc. Used to set and query the exception’s error type.

Thread-safe-ish singleton-capable output utility used by Apache Thrift to print or report messages. Provides a configurable output function callback, printf-style formatting, perror helpers that avoid allocating when given const char*, a static error-time wrapper, and a strerror_s helper returning std::string. Holds a function pointer f_ used to emit messages. Construction details and default callback are defined elsewhere (not in this header).

Opaque, fixed-size UUID wrapper storing 16 bytes in network order. Provides construction from a 16-byte array, from a string UUID (various canonical formats), and optionally from boost::uuids::uuid. Supports iteration over raw bytes, size query, data access, swap, nil check, and equality/inequality. Intended for representing and serializing UUIDs in Thrift code. Destruction has no special requirements. Copyable and movable.

Abstract callback interface for observing processor lifecycle events (context creation/free, pre/post read/write, async completion, and error). Subclass to hook into processing; default implementations are no-ops.
RAII helper that frees a context via TProcessorEventHandler::freeContext in its destructor unless unregistered. Used by generated code to ensure context cleanup.
Abstract processor that reads requests from an input TProtocol and writes responses to an output TProtocol. Supports an optional TProcessorEventHandler for instrumentation.
Connection metadata provided to factories when creating a TProcessor: input/output protocols and the accepted transport backing the connection.
Abstract factory interface that produces a TProcessor for a given connection. getProcessor is called in the accepting thread.
Concrete TProcessorFactory that always returns the same TProcessor instance supplied at construction time.

Non-templated dispatching processor base. Reads the Thrift message header and invokes an abstract dispatchCall() implemented by subclasses. Also serves as the specialization target for TDispatchProcessorT<protocol::TProtocol> and <protocol::TDummyProtocol>.

Abstract base class for Thrift-generated structs/objects that can serialize/deserialize themselves using a TProtocol. It declares pure-virtual read and write methods and a virtual destructor. Implementations are expected to read from and write to Apache Thrift protocols. Details such as error handling and ownership of protocol objects are not specified here.

A constant object of type std::locale initialized with the classic "C" locale used to imbue string streams for deterministic number formatting. It has internal linkage due to the unnamed namespace. Note: While this is a variable and not a type definition, no custom structs/enums/typedefs/classes are defined in this header; thus, there are no custom data types to document beyond standard library types referenced here.

A small base class intended to be inherited by other classes to disable copy construction and copy assignment. It provides a protected default constructor and virtual destructor, and explicitly deletes the copy constructor and copy-assignment operator. Move operations are not declared here, so they follow compiler defaults (typically allowed if not otherwise impeded by members). Intended usage: derive publicly or privately to make the derived class non-copyable.

Abstract base class for Thrift protocol drivers. Defines the full virtual interface for reading and writing Thrift types, plus recursion-depth tracking and access to the underlying transport. Must be subclassed by concrete protocols (e.g., binary, compact).
Abstract factory for constructing protocol instances from transports. Implementations choose concrete protocol type and configuration.

objects.definition: class TDummyProtocol : public TProtocol {};
objects.description: Placeholder protocol used by code generators; provides no functionality and should not be instantiated at runtime.
Utility type providing static helpers to convert 16/32/64-bit integers to and from network (big-endian) byte order using platform primitives.
Utility type providing static helpers to convert integers to and from little-endian wire order. Typically faster than big-endian path on little-endian hosts.
RAII helper that increments a TProtocol's output recursion depth on construction and decrements it on destruction to enforce recursion limits safely.
RAII helper that increments a TProtocol's input recursion depth on construction and decrements it on destruction to enforce recursion limits safely.

Exception class for Apache Thrift protocol-layer errors. It extends apache::thrift::TException and encapsulates a TProtocolExceptionType code plus an optional message. The what() string derives from the message if provided, otherwise from the type_. Construction typically uses a specific error type or a message. Destruction is noexcept. Ownership/lifecycle is standard C++ exception semantics; no special destruction is required beyond normal RAII.
Strongly-scoped enumeration (as a nested enum within TProtocolException) classifying protocol error categories, used to initialize and query the type of a TProtocolException.

Templated Thrift binary protocol implementation. Provides read/write methods for Thrift primitives and containers over a Transport_ with a selectable network byte order. Supports configurable size limits and strict versioned messages. This is the core protocol class used by the typedefs TBinaryProtocol and TLEBinaryProtocol.

Factory for creating TBinaryProtocolT instances with preset size limits and strictness flags. Chooses a protocol specialized for the concrete Transport_ if possible, otherwise falls back to base TTransport.

Concrete Thrift protocol that reads/writes data in JSON wire format. Provides read/write methods for all Thrift primitive and container types, message framing, and minimal-size checks. Manages parsing context stack and a byte lookahead reader over an underlying TTransport. Construction requires a transport. Destruction/ownership of the transport is external.
Helper class nested in TJSONProtocol that allows peeking a single next byte from a TTransport without consuming it, or consuming it if already peeked. Maintains one-byte buffer and state.
Factory for creating TJSONProtocol instances from a transport. Provides defaulted constructor and destructor and overrides getProtocol to return a new TJSONProtocol.
Forward-declared context type used internally by TJSONProtocol to manage JSON reading/writing state (e.g., arrays/objects). Definition is not present in this header; details unknown.

Decorator class for apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol that forwards all read/write operations to an underlying TProtocol instance. Useful as a base for concrete protocol decorators (e.g., multiplexing, logging). Lifetime: holds a shared_ptr to the wrapped protocol; transport is taken from the wrapped protocol in the constructor. No additional state or ownership beyond the shared_ptr.

Concrete helper subclass of apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol that supplies default (throwing) implementations of all read/write methods. Intended as a base for TVirtualProtocol to avoid infinite recursion in non-overridden non-virtual methods. Not intended for direct use; construct with a TTransport and override methods in derived concrete protocols.

Concrete protocol decorator that prefixes the service name to outgoing RPC method names so a single transport can multiplex multiple Thrift services. It wraps another TProtocol and modifies writeMessageBegin to prepend "serviceName:method". The serviceName and separator are stored as immutable strings. Destruction is defaulted; lifecycle is tied to the wrapped protocol via TProtocolDecorator. Server-side code should not use this class.

objects.definition:
namespace apache {
namespace thrift {
namespace protocol {

/**
 * Enumerated definition of the types that the Thrift protocol supports.
 * Take special note of the T_END type which is used specifically to mark
 * the end of a sequence of fields.
 */
enum TType {
  T_STOP       = 0,
  T_VOID       = 1,
  T_BOOL       = 2,
  T_BYTE       = 3,
  T_I08        = 3,
  T_I16        = 6,
  T_I32        = 8,
  T_U64        = 9,
  T_I64        = 10,
  T_DOUBLE     = 4,
  T_STRING     = 11,
  T_UTF7       = 11,
  T_STRUCT     = 12,
  T_MAP        = 13,
  T_SET        = 14,
  T_LIST       = 15,
  T_UUID       = 16,
};

}}} // apache::thrift::protocol
objects.description: Enumeration of the Thrift wire types used by the apache::thrift::protocol layer. Values identify the kind of field (stop, void, bool, various integers, double, string/UTF7, struct, map, set, list, uuid). Note: T_BYTE and T_I08 are aliases with the same value (3); T_STRING and T_UTF7 are aliases with the same value (11).
Enumeration of Thrift message types: call, reply, exception, and oneway. Used to mark the kind of RPC message on the wire.

A small value-type class in apache::thrift::protocol that carries list metadata for Thrift protocols: the element type (TType) and the list size. Defaults to T_STOP and 0. Intended to be used when reading/writing list headers in Thrift serialization.

A small value-type class in apache::thrift::protocol that carries metadata for a Thrift map field: the key type, value type (both TType from TEnum.h), and the element count. Provides a default constructor initializing types to T_STOP and size to 0, and a value constructor to set key/value types and size. Used when reading/writing map headers in Thrift protocols; does not manage memory for map contents.

Metadata holder for Thrift set types. Stores the element type (TType) and the declared/encoded size. Provides constructors for default, from element type and size, and from a TList (copying element type and size). Intended for protocol implementations to describe set containers; does not own any elements and has no dynamic resources.

Abstract base class for Thrift transports. Provides default behaviors and throwing stubs for read/write/open/close/flush/borrow/consume. Tracks message size limits via TConfiguration to protect against oversized messages. Intended to be subclassed by concrete transports (e.g., sockets, buffers).

Factory interface for wrapping or producing TTransport instances. Default implementation returns the provided transport unchanged; subclasses may decorate or replace transports for server-side input/output handling.

Exception class for transport-layer errors in Apache Thrift. It categorizes transport failures via an internal TTransportExceptionType enum and carries an explanatory message. It derives from apache::thrift::TException, overrides what(), and stores the error type. Constructors allow specifying type, message, and an errno-based message suffix. Use getType() to branch on error category.

objects.definition:
enum TTransportExceptionType {
    UNKNOWN = 0,
    NOT_OPEN = 1,
    TIMED_OUT = 2,
    END_OF_FILE = 3,
    INTERRUPTED = 4,
    BAD_ARGS = 5,
    CORRUPTED_DATA = 6,
    INTERNAL_ERROR = 7,
    CLIENT_DISCONNECT = 8
  };
objects.description: Enumeration of transport error categories used by TTransportException to classify failures (e.g., NOT_OPEN, TIMED_OUT, END_OF_FILE).

A no-op transport analogous to /dev/null. Always appears open; read operations (inherited defaults) yield no data, and write() accepts data but discards it. Useful in testing or disabling output sinks.

A transport that mirrors traffic between a source transport and a destination transport, buffering the entire request/response. It can pipe on readEnd (default) and/or on writeEnd, forwarding accumulated data to dstTrans_. Manages dynamic internal read/write buffers and delegates open/close to the source transport.
Factory that wraps an input transport into a TPipedTransport that pipes to a pre-initialized destination transport. initializeTargetTransport must be called at most once; subsequent calls throw.

A piped transport specialized for file-reader sources. Inherits TPipedTransport and TFileReaderTransport, exposing file-reader specific controls (timeouts, chunking, seeking) while piping reads/writes to a destination transport. Requires a TFileReaderTransport as source.

Factory that creates TPipedFileReaderTransport instances from an existing TFileReaderTransport source and a pre-configured destination transport. Overrides getTransport to only wrap sources that are TFileReaderTransport-compatible.

Abstract base class providing fast-path buffered read/write/borrow operations backed by internal pointers. Subclasses implement slow-path methods when buffers underflow/overflow. Intended for high-performance transports.
Buffered transport that reads into and writes from internal heap buffers to minimize system calls. Defers I/O to an underlying TTransport. Provides flush and borrow semantics.
Factory that wraps an existing TTransport in a TBufferedTransport.
Length-prefixed framed transport. Writes accumulate in a buffer and flush() emits a 4-byte frame size followed by payload. Reads are done frame-by-frame with maximum frame size enforcement.
Factory that wraps an existing TTransport in a TFramedTransport.
In-memory transport using a growable buffer. Can observe, copy, or take ownership of external memory via MemoryPolicy. Suitable for testing, buffering, or in-process transports.

objects.definition: enum MemoryPolicy { OBSERVE = 1, COPY = 2, TAKE_OWNERSHIP = 3 };
objects.description: Enumeration defined inside TMemoryBuffer that controls how externally provided buffers are handled: observe without writing, copy into owned storage, or take ownership of malloc-allocated memory.

Concrete transport implementing a TCP (and Unix domain) socket for Apache Thrift. Provides connection management, timeouts, socket options, read/write, and cached peer info. Inherits from TVirtualTransport<TSocket>. Lifetime: construct, optionally configure (host/port/path, timeouts, options), open(), use read/write, then close() or let destructor close. Thread-safety is not documented; likely not thread-safe for concurrent I/O.
Strongly-typed enum describing what kind of socket a TServerSocket is or should be bound to: none, IPv4 (INET), IPv6 (INET6), or Unix domain (UNIX).

Server-side transport implementing a listening socket for Thrift servers. Wraps OS listen/accept on TCP/IPv4, TCP/IPv6, or Unix domain sockets. Provides configuration for timeouts, backlog, keepalive, buffer sizes, interruptability, and custom setsockopt callbacks on the listening and accepted sockets.

Represents a single backend server entry used by TSocketPool. Holds host/port identity plus connection health state (last failure time and consecutive failure count) and an associated socket handle. Constructors allow default or host/port initialization. No ownership semantics are implied; instances are typically managed via std::shared_ptr by TSocketPool.

A TSocket-derived transport that manages a pool of backend servers and implements retry, backoff, and randomized selection policies. Provides multiple constructors to seed the pool, and setters for retry behavior. open() selects/opens a server; close() shuts down the current connection. Instances own a list of shared_ptr<TSocketPoolServer> and track the current server and retry policy state.

HTTP-based client transport class extending THttpTransport. It can either wrap an existing TTransport or construct its own socket transport from a host and port. It manages HTTP request/response formatting, including Host and path headers, and overrides flush() to send buffered data via HTTP, as well as header/status parsing methods. Details of connection handling and exact HTTP formatting are defined in the base class and implementation file.

HTTP server-side transport that wraps an underlying TTransport with HTTP semantics. It derives from THttpTransport and overrides parsing and flushing behaviors, adding helpers for header construction, header/status parsing, and RFC1123 time formatting. Used to speak HTTP when serving Thrift requests. Destruction/ownership semantics follow base THttpTransport; constructed with an underlying transport and optional configuration.

Factory for producing THttpServer-wrapped transports. Provides getTransport that takes an existing TTransport and returns a new THttpServer around it, enabling HTTP semantics for server-side transport. Destructor and constructor are trivial/default.

Concrete HTTP/1.1 transport implementing the Thrift transport interface, layered over another TTransport. Handles request/response framing, headers, 100-Continue, chunked transfer, content-length, and keepalive. It buffers writes and reads via TMemoryBuffer and requires subclasses to implement HTTP-specific parsing via parseHeader and parseStatusLine. Construction wraps an existing underlying transport and optional configuration.

Concrete transport that wraps a native POSIX file descriptor and exposes the Thrift TTransport API. It can optionally close the descriptor on destruction according to ClosePolicy. Methods provide basic open/close/read/write operations; open() is a no-op here. Ownership of the FD is controlled by the ClosePolicy.

objects.definition: enum ClosePolicy { NO_CLOSE_ON_DESTROY = 0, CLOSE_ON_DESTROY = 1 };
objects.description: Enumeration embedded in TFDTransport controlling whether the file descriptor should be closed when the TFDTransport is destroyed. NO_CLOSE_ON_DESTROY leaves the FD open; CLOSE_ON_DESTROY closes it in the destructor.

On Windows, TPipe is a concrete TVirtualTransport implementing Thrift transport over Windows named or anonymous pipes. It supports construction from existing HANDLEs, TAutoHandle, or a pipe name, and provides open/close/read/write and metadata accessors. On non-Windows platforms, TPipe is an alias of TSocket, meaning pipe semantics are not provided here and it behaves as a socket transport. Do not destroy a TPipe at global scope on Windows to avoid DLLMain thread joins. Construction and lifetime are managed by the class; underlying OS handles are owned by the instance once set.

Server-side transport that accepts connections via Windows Named Pipes (and anonymous pipes) when built on Windows. Provides TServerTransport interface: listen, accept (via acceptImpl), close, interrupt, and accessors for pipe configuration and native HANDLEs. On non-Windows builds, TPipeServer is an alias of TServerSocket, serving as a Unix-domain socket-based stand-in. Construction details: multiple constructors allow named or anonymous pipes, buffer sizing, max connections, and a security descriptor. Internals are implemented via a pimpl (TPipeServerImpl). Destruction likely closes pipe handles and joins any worker thread; avoid global-scope destruction per header comment.
direct_api_constructors: apache::thrift::transport::TPipeServer::TPipeServer(const std::string& pipename, uint32_t bufsize, uint32_t maxconnections)
apache::thrift::transport::TPipeServer::TPipeServer(const std::string& pipename, uint32_t bufsize, uint32_t maxconnections, const std::string& securityDescriptor)

objects.definition: class TPipe;
objects.description: Forward declaration for a pipe-related class used alongside TPipeServer on Windows. The actual definition is not present in this header.

Concrete transport class that wraps a filesystem file using the TFDTransport base. Intended for simple file-based I/O; when opened for writing it uses O_CREAT and O_APPEND semantics. Only the constructor is declared here; full behavior is defined in the implementation file. Details such as lifecycle, ownership of file descriptors, and exact open flags beyond O_CREAT/O_APPEND are not shown in this header.
direct_api_constructors: apache::thrift::transport::TSimpleFileTransport::TSimpleFileTransport(const std::string& path, bool read, bool write, std::shared_ptr<TConfiguration> config)

objects.description: A testing transport that wraps another TTransport and randomly shortens reads to simulate partial reads. It derives from TVirtualTransport<TShortReadTransport>, forwarding most operations to the underlying transport. The probability full_prob controls how often a read passes through with full requested length; otherwise a smaller random length is used. It tracks read/consumed bytes via TVirtualTransport helpers.

Nonblocking server-side transport that wraps a listening socket (TCP or Unix domain) and implements TNonblockingServerTransport. Manages listen/accept, socket options, timeouts, and provides callbacks for customizing setsockopt on the listening and accepted sockets. Internally stores socket descriptors, address/port or path, and configuration like backlog, keepalive, buffer sizes, and retry behavior.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void(THRIFT_SOCKET fd)> socket_func_t;
objects.description: Alias type for a callback functor invoked with a socket descriptor. Used for listen and accept customization callbacks within TNonblockingServerSocket.

Abstract base class for a nonblocking server-side transport within Apache Thrift. It defines the interface for listening, accepting new TSocket connections, retrieving the underlying server socket descriptor and port information, and closing the transport. Subclasses must implement acceptImpl(), getSocketFD(), getPort(), getListenPort(), and close(). listen() has a default no-op implementation that can be overridden. The class enforces that accept() never returns nullptr by throwing TTransportException if acceptImpl() does.

Abstract callback interface for server lifecycle and per-connection/per-request events. Users subclass it to observe and manage contexts around serving, client connection processing, and cleanup. No ownership semantics are imposed; typically installed on a TServer via setServerEventHandler.

Abstract base class for Thrift servers. Provides constructors to wire processor factories, transports, and protocol factories; exposes serve/stop lifecycle and integrates with Runnable::run. Concrete servers derive from this and implement serve(). Holds shared_ptr-owned collaborators and an optional TServerEventHandler.

Helper function declaration to raise the process file descriptor limit. Only declared when HAVE_SYS_RESOURCE_H is defined. Not a type; included here only for completeness per header content. Note: This is a function, not a data type.

Abstract server framework base class providing a unified accept/process loop for Thrift servers. It handles client acceptance, tracking of concurrent clients with a monitor, and exposes hooks for subclasses to react to client connect/disconnect events. Maintains current, high-watermark, and limit counters for concurrent clients. Construction takes processor and transport/protocol factories or instances. Destruction and lifecycle specifics beyond declarations are defined in the corresponding implementation file.

Concrete single-threaded server implementation in Apache Thrift that processes one client connection at a time using the TServerFramework base. Provides multiple constructors to configure processor(s), transports, and protocols. Overrides lifecycle hooks for client connect/disconnect and hides concurrent-client limit (fixed to single client). Implementation details are not present in this header.

Concrete Thrift server that accepts client connections and hands each request off to a ThreadManager-managed thread pool. It derives from TServerFramework and exposes configuration for request timeout and task expiration. The actual behavior (serve loop, client lifecycle hooks) is defined in the corresponding implementation file.
direct_api_constructors: apache::thrift::server::TThreadPoolServer::TThreadPoolServer(const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::TProcessorFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TServerTransport>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TTransportFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TTransportFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::concurrency::ThreadManager>&)

apache::thrift::server::TThreadPoolServer::TThreadPoolServer(const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::TProcessor>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TServerTransport>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TTransportFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::transport::TTransportFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolFactory>&, const std::shared_ptr<apache::thrift::concurrency::ThreadManager>&)

objects.description: A threaded Thrift server implementation that spawns one thread per client and cleans them up when the client disconnects. It extends TServerFramework and manages client connections, lifecycle, and per-client threads via a ThreadFactory and Monitor. Construction supports multiple overloads for processor and transport/protocol factory wiring.

A Runnable representing a single client connection handled by a Thrift TServer. It owns protocol/transport endpoints and an event handler to process requests in a loop within run(), and performs resource cleanup via cleanup(). Construction requires a processor, input/output protocols, an event handler, and the client transport. Destruction and cleanup close protocols/transports and release any event handler context. Details of processing are defined in the referenced Thrift components; this header does not expose additional lifecycle constraints beyond Runnable::run().

Abstract interface for asynchronously processing buffered Thrift data. Implementations read from an input buffer and write results to an output buffer, then invoke the supplied completion callback with a boolean indicating connection health. Intended to operate on in-memory buffer transports (e.g., TMemoryBuffer), not directly on socket wrappers.

Abstract base class defining an asynchronous message channel in Apache Thrift. Implementations send and receive messages using TMemoryBuffer and invoke the provided completion callback (VoidCallback) upon operation completion. It exposes state query methods (good, error, timedOut). sendAndRecvMessage has a provided virtual declaration here (likely with a default implementation elsewhere) allowing a request/response flow built atop sendMessage/recvMessage.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void()> VoidCallback;
objects.description: Type alias for a no-argument, void-returning callback used by TAsyncChannel to notify completion of send/receive operations. This is a typedef nested inside TAsyncChannel.

Non-templated async dispatch processor that reads the message header and then delegates dispatch to a derived-class implementation via dispatchCall. Does not attempt protocol dynamic_cast optimization.

Explicit specializations of TAsyncDispatchProcessorT for protocol::TDummyProtocol and protocol::TProtocol that alias the behavior to the non-templated TAsyncDispatchProcessor. These provide compatibility paths that skip dynamic_cast and use the generic dispatch implementation.

Abstract base class for asynchronous Thrift processors. Implementations perform request handling asynchronously and must invoke the supplied completion callback when finished. Holds an optional TProcessorEventHandler used for instrumentation or hooks. Note: TProcessorEventHandler and TConnectionInfo are referenced from other headers and are not defined here.

Abstract factory for creating TAsyncProcessor instances per connection. getProcessor is invoked on the acceptor thread and returns a processor to handle requests for the given connection. TConnectionInfo is referenced but not defined here.

Asynchronous buffer processor that adapts an underlying TAsyncProcessor to use protocol-based processing via a provided TProtocolFactory. It constructs input/output protocols from buffer transports and delegates request handling to the underlying processor. Lifecycle and exact processing details are not shown here; destructor is defaulted. The class is defined in this header; referenced base class (TAsyncBufferProcessor) and other types are declared in included headers.

RAII helper for send-side synchronization. On construction it associates with a TConcurrentClientSyncInfo to manage write/send critical sections; commit() marks successful completion. Destructor likely releases or rolls back if not committed.

RAII helper for receive-side synchronization tied to a specific sequence id. Works with TConcurrentClientSyncInfo to coordinate waiting for and handling a response. commit() indicates successful processing; destructor performs cleanup/unblock if not committed.

Synchronization state for a concurrent Thrift client. Manages sequence IDs, per-request monitors, and read/write mutexes to coordinate sending and receiving across multiple in-flight calls. Provides methods to generate sequence IDs, update/get pending message info, and wait for work. Internal helpers manage monitor cache and error signaling.

Client channel implementation that adapts libevent's HTTP facilities to Thrift's TAsyncChannel interface. Manages an evhttp_connection and queues callbacks/buffers for send/receive over HTTP to a specified host/path. Exact wire details are not shown here; behavior must be inferred from method names and member fields.

objects.definition: struct event_base;
objects.description: Forward declaration of libevent's event loop base structure. Only declared here; the full definition resides in libevent headers. Used by TEvhttpServer to manage event processing. Details unknown in this header.

objects.definition: struct evhttp;
objects.description: Forward declaration of libevent's HTTP server handle. Only declared here; full definition is in libevent. Used internally by TEvhttpServer to accept and handle HTTP requests.

objects.definition: struct evhttp_request;
objects.description: Forward declaration of libevent's HTTP request object. Only declared here; full definition is in libevent. Passed to TEvhttpServer::request and process callbacks.

objects.definition: class TAsyncBufferProcessor;
objects.description: Forward-declared processor interface/class responsible for processing Thrift requests buffered over HTTP. Only declared here; definition is elsewhere in the Thrift codebase.

Asynchronous HTTP server bridge for Thrift using libevent. Can be constructed to integrate with an external evhttp or manage its own event_base/evhttp. Exposes a static request callback for evhttp, a serve loop for embedded mode, and access to the event base. Internally holds a TAsyncBufferProcessor and libevent handles. The nested RequestContext is only forward-declared here; its definition is not provided in this header.

objects.definition: class NoSuchTaskException : public apache::thrift::TException {};
objects.description: Exception type indicating that an operation referenced a task that does not exist. Inherits from apache::thrift::TException. No additional state or behavior.

objects.definition: class UncancellableTaskException : public apache::thrift::TException {};
objects.description: Exception thrown when an attempt to cancel a task fails because the task cannot be cancelled. Inherits from apache::thrift::TException. No additional state or behavior.

objects.definition: class InvalidArgumentException : public apache::thrift::TException {};
objects.description: Exception indicating an invalid or out-of-range argument was supplied to a concurrency API. Inherits from apache::thrift::TException. No additional state or behavior.
Exception indicating that an operation was invoked in an illegal or unexpected state. Provides default and message-taking constructors; otherwise inherits behavior from apache::thrift::TException.
Exception indicating a timeout occurred while waiting on a concurrency operation. Supplies a default message and a custom-message constructor. Inherits from apache::thrift::TException.
Exception thrown when a scheduler or executor has exceeded its limit of pending tasks. Provides default and message-taking constructors; inherits from apache::thrift::TException.
Exception indicating system resource exhaustion or related failures (e.g., threads, memory). Provides default and message constructors; inherits from apache::thrift::TException.

A Runnable implementation that executes user-provided callbacks. It can run a single-shot void(void) function, adapt a pthread-style void*(void*) function (discarding its return), or repeatedly invoke a bool(void) function at a fixed millisecond interval until it returns false.

objects.definition: typedef void* (*PthreadFuncPtr)(void* arg);
objects.description: Type alias for a pthread_create-style function pointer taking a void* argument and returning void*. Used by FunctionRunner to wrap such callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void()> VoidFunc;
objects.description: Alias for a callable with signature void(). Used by FunctionRunner for single-shot execution.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<bool()> BoolFunc;
objects.description: Alias for a callable with signature bool(). When provided to FunctionRunner with an interval, it is executed repeatedly until it returns false.

Monitor combines a mutex with a condition variable-like interface. It provides locking, timed/untimed waits, and notification, implementing logical constness. It may either own an internal mutex or wrap an external one; ownership affects destruction behavior. Internal implementation details are hidden behind an opaque nested class Impl and a pointer impl_.

Synchronized is an RAII helper that locks a Monitor’s underlying mutex for the lifetime of the Synchronized object via an internal Guard. It acquires the lock in the constructor using the Monitor’s mutex(). Destruction semantics depend on Guard, which is defined in Mutex.h. The header does not expose explicit unlock; scope exit releases the lock.

A simple mutex class that provides lock, trylock, timed lock, and unlock operations. It uses a pimpl (private implementation) via a shared_ptr to an internal impl class. All methods are declared const and operate on the internal implementation. The underlying implementation may throw exceptions on failure. Construction allocates/initializes the implementation; destruction is defaulted. getUnderlyingImpl exposes a raw pointer to the underlying implementation object for integration with platform APIs.

RAII locking guard for Mutex. On construction, locks the provided Mutex according to timeout semantics: timeout==0 blocks; timeout<0 attempts a non-blocking trylock; timeout>0 attempts a timed lock for the specified milliseconds. If locking fails (non-blocking or timed-out), the guard becomes disengaged (mutex_==nullptr) and its bool conversion is false. On destruction, unlocks the held mutex if engaged. Inherits from TNonCopyable to prevent copying.

Abstract base class representing a unit of work to be executed by a Thread. Similar to Java's Runnable; classes derive from Runnable and implement run(). Maintains a weak reference to the hosting Thread, accessible via thread() and settable by Thread implementations.

Supports detached or joinable operation. Uses Monitor/Synchronized for coordination and a static threadMain entry point selected by getThreadFunc().

A factory class in apache::thrift::concurrency that creates Thread instances bound to a Runnable. It manages whether created threads are detached or joinable via an internal detached_ flag. Threads are returned as std::shared_ptr and the API suggests proper cleanup occurs when references are released. The concrete behavior of newThread and getCurrentThreadId is defined elsewhere.

Abstract interface for a thread pool manager within apache::thrift::concurrency. It owns and coordinates a pool of worker threads created via a ThreadFactory, manages task queues, supports limits, expiration callbacks, and exposes lifecycle control (start/stop) and metrics. Concrete implementations are provided elsewhere. Nested forward declarations Task, Worker, and Impl indicate internal helper/implementation types.

Returns the result of dispatchCall, or false if the message type is invalid.
requirements: in must be a non-null std::shared_ptr to a valid apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol instance capable of readMessageBegin().
out must be a non-null std::shared_ptr to a valid apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol instance appropriate for writing the reply (or for oneway calls).

The incoming message read from 'in' must begin with a valid Thrift message header; the message type must be apache::thrift::protocol::T_CALL or apache::thrift::protocol::T_ONEWAY. Any other type causes the function to return false.
A subclass must implement dispatchCall(apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol*, apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol*, const std::string&, int32_t, void*); otherwise linking will fail.
connectionContext may be null; no specific format is required by this function (it is forwarded to dispatchers).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not guaranteed by this function; callers must ensure appropriate synchronization if shared across threads (not specified by the header).

requirements: May be invoked implicitly when an apache::thrift::TBase-derived object goes out of scope or is deleted via a base pointer.

functions.name: apache::thrift::TBase::read

requirements: iprot must be a non-null pointer to a valid apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol instance.
The protocol must be positioned at the beginning of this object's serialized representation and contain data compatible with the derived type's expected schema.
The call modifies the state of the receiving object to reflect the decoded data.
Callers should use a concrete derived type (TBase is abstract); this function cannot be called directly on TBase.
Error handling (exceptions or error codes) is not specified in this header; callers should follow the concrete implementation's contract in the corresponding generated/implementation files.

requirements: oprot must be a non-null pointer to a valid apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocol instance.

Formatting is done using the "C" locale (e.g., decimal separator is '.')

functions.name: apache::thrift::to_string

requirements: t must be a valid float value; special values (NaN/Inf) are streamed according to iostream rules.
The referenced t must be valid during the call.
Formatting uses the "C" locale; precision is set to ceil(digits*log10(2)+1).

functions.description: Performs a bitwise reinterpretation of a value of type From as a value of type To, requiring both types to have identical size. functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TBinaryProtocolFactoryT::getProtocol
functions.signature:
template <class Transport_, class ByteOrder_>
std::shared_ptr<TProtocol> TBinaryProtocolFactoryT<Transport_, ByteOrder_>::getProtocol(std::shared_ptr<TTransport> trans)
functions.description: Creates a TBinaryProtocolT instance bound to the given transport. If trans can be dynamically cast to Transport_, constructs a protocol with that specific transport type; otherwise falls back to using TTransport.
requirements: trans should be a non-null shared_ptr to an open transport ready for I/O.
Returned shared_ptr owns the created protocol; caller should keep it alive for the duration of use.
Thread-safety follows that of the underlying transport; do not share across threads unless transport/protocol are designed for it.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeMessageBegin
functions.signature: virtual uint32_t writeMessageBegin(const std::string& name, const TMessageType messageType, const int32_t seqid);
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift message using the Compact Protocol. Writes the protocol header/version and message envelope (name, type, sequence id). Call before writing any structs or fields for the message.
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent writeMessageEnd() for the same message.
messageType must be a valid TMessageType value.
Call before writing any message payload (structs/fields).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeStructBegin
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift struct. Prepares internal state for field id delta encoding used by the Compact Protocol.
requirements: Must be paired with a corresponding writeStructEnd().
Call before writing fields of the struct with writeFieldBegin()/write...().
name is not transmitted on the wire (per Thrift conventions) and may be ignored by the protocol.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeStructEnd
functions.description: Ends a previously started struct write. Finalizes any internal state for delta field ids.
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching writeStructBegin().
All intended fields should be written before calling writeStructEnd().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeFieldBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t writeFieldBegin(const char* name, const TType fieldType, const int16_t fieldId);
functions.description: Begins writing a field within a struct. Emits the field header using Compact Protocol encoding. For boolean fields, header emission may be deferred until the value is known.
requirements: Must be called between writeStructBegin() and writeStructEnd().
fieldType must be a valid TType for the field.
fieldId should correspond to the field id defined in the Thrift IDL and fit in int16_t.
For boolean fields, the actual header may be combined with the value written by writeBool().
After the field value is written, a writeFieldEnd() may be called (no-op in this implementation).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeFieldStop
functions.description: Writes the Compact Protocol STOP marker indicating the end of fields in the current struct.
requirements: Must be called after the last field of a struct and before writeStructEnd().
Only valid within an active struct (between writeStructBegin() and writeStructEnd()).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeListBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t writeListBegin(const TType elemType, const uint32_t size);
functions.description: Begins writing a list container header with the given element type and element count using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: Must be followed by writing exactly 'size' list elements of type elemType, then a writeListEnd().
elemType must be a valid TType for list elements.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeSetBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t writeSetBegin(const TType elemType, const uint32_t size);
functions.description: Begins writing a set container header with the given element type and element count using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: Must be followed by writing exactly 'size' set elements of type elemType, then a writeSetEnd().
elemType must be a valid TType for set elements.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeMapBegin
functions.signature: virtual uint32_t writeMapBegin(const TType keyType, const TType valType, const uint32_t size);
functions.description: Begins writing a map container header with the given key and value types and the entry count using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: Must be followed by writing exactly 'size' key/value pairs, then a writeMapEnd().
keyType and valType must be valid TType values for keys and values.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeBool
functions.description: Writes a boolean value. For boolean struct fields, may also finalize a previously deferred field header by embedding the value into the header as per Compact Protocol.
requirements: If used immediately after writeFieldBegin() for a boolean field, this will complete the field header encoding.
May be used for container elements or standalone values as appropriate for the surrounding context.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeByte
functions.description: Writes an 8-bit integer value using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: Value must fit in int8_t.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeI16
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit integer using Compact Protocol zigzag + varint encoding.
requirements: Value must fit in int16_t.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeI32
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit integer using Compact Protocol zigzag + varint encoding.
requirements: Value must fit in int32_t.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeI64
functions.description: Writes a 64-bit integer using Compact Protocol zigzag + varint encoding.
requirements: Value must fit in int64_t.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeDouble
functions.description: Writes a double-precision floating-point value using Compact Protocol encoding (IEEE 754 binary64).
requirements: Value must be a finite double if the receiving side expects finite numbers (protocol does not itself forbid NaN/Inf, but downstream consumers may).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeString
functions.description: Writes a UTF-8 string as a length-prefixed binary using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: str.size() must fit in the protocol's length encoding (uint32 length in practice).
String contents are transmitted as raw bytes; caller is responsible for providing valid UTF-8 if required by the IDL.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeBinary
functions.description: Writes a binary blob as a length-prefixed sequence of bytes using Compact Protocol encoding.
requirements: str.size() must fit in the protocol's length encoding (uint32 length in practice).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeUUID
functions.description: Writes a UUID value using Compact Protocol encoding for UUIDs.
requirements: The provided TUuid must be properly initialized/formatted for this implementation's expected UUID wire format.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::getMinSerializedSize
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of bytes that a value of the given TType could occupy when encoded with the Compact Protocol. Used to conservatively preflight read availability.
requirements: type must be a valid TType.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::checkReadBytesAvailable
functions.description: Checks that the underlying transport has enough bytes available to read a set with the given element type and size, using a conservative minimum-size estimate per element.
requirements: set.size_ must be the number of elements expected to be read.
set.elemType_ must be a valid TType.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeMessageEnd
functions.description: Ends writing a Thrift message. No wire data is emitted by this method in the Compact Protocol implementation provided here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching writeMessageBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeMapEnd
functions.description: Ends writing a map container. No wire data is emitted by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching writeMapBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeListEnd
functions.description: Ends writing a list container. No wire data is emitted by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching writeListBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeSetEnd
functions.description: Ends writing a set container. No wire data is emitted by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching writeSetBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::writeFieldEnd
functions.description: Ends writing a field. No wire data is emitted by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be called after the corresponding field's value is written (optional, as it is a no-op).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readMessageBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t readMessageBegin(std::string& name, TMessageType& messageType, int32_t& seqid);
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift message using the Compact Protocol. Parses and returns the message envelope (protocol header/version, name, type, sequence id).
requirements: name, messageType, and seqid must be valid references to receive outputs.
Must be paired with a subsequent readMessageEnd() for the same message.
Call before reading any message payload (structs/fields).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readStructBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift struct. Initializes internal state for delta field id decoding.
requirements: name must be a valid reference to receive the (optional) struct name; Compact Protocol may not transmit the name, so it may be empty.
Must be paired with readStructEnd().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readStructEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a Thrift struct. Finalizes internal state for field id tracking.
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching readStructBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readFieldBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t readFieldBegin(std::string& name, TType& fieldType, int16_t& fieldId);
functions.description: Begins reading a field header within a struct. Decodes and returns the field type and id. For boolean fields, the value may be embedded in the header and cached for readBool().
requirements: Must be called between readStructBegin() and readStructEnd().
name, fieldType, and fieldId must be valid references to receive outputs.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readMapBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t readMapBegin(TType& keyType, TType& valType, uint32_t& size);
functions.description: Begins reading a map container header. Decodes key/value types and entry count.
requirements: keyType, valType, and size must be valid references to receive outputs.
Must be paired with readMapEnd() after reading the entries.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readListBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a list container header. Decodes element type and element count.
requirements: elemType and size must be valid references to receive outputs.
Must be paired with readListEnd() after reading the elements.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readSetBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a set container header. Decodes element type and element count.
requirements: elemType and size must be valid references to receive outputs.
Must be paired with readSetEnd() after reading the elements.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readBool
functions.description: Reads a boolean value. For boolean fields, may consume a value embedded in the previously read field header.
requirements: value must be a valid reference to receive the boolean.
Must be called in a context where a boolean is expected (e.g., after an appropriate field or within a container).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readByte
functions.description: Reads an 8-bit integer value.
requirements: byte must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readI16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit integer value encoded with Compact Protocol (zigzag + varint).
requirements: i16 must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readI32
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit integer value encoded with Compact Protocol (zigzag + varint).
requirements: i32 must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readI64
functions.description: Reads a 64-bit integer value encoded with Compact Protocol (zigzag + varint).
requirements: i64 must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readDouble
functions.description: Reads a double-precision floating-point value.
requirements: dub must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readString
functions.description: Reads a length-prefixed string (raw bytes) and stores it in str. Subject to the protocol's configured string size limit.
requirements: str must be a valid reference to receive the result.
If a string size limit is configured (string_limit_), the incoming length must not exceed it (enforced internally).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readBinary
functions.description: Reads a length-prefixed binary blob and stores it in str. Subject to the protocol's configured string size limit.
requirements: str must be a valid reference to receive the result.
If a string size limit is configured (string_limit_), the incoming length must not exceed it (enforced internally).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readUUID
functions.description: Reads a UUID value using the Compact Protocol's UUID wire format and stores it in the provided TUuid.
requirements: str must be a valid reference to receive the parsed UUID.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readMessageEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a Thrift message. No wire data is consumed by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching readMessageBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readFieldEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a field. No wire data is consumed by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be called after the corresponding field value has been read (optional, as it is a no-op).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readMapEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a map container. No wire data is consumed by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching readMapBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readListEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a list container. No wire data is consumed by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching readListBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolT::readSetEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a set container. No wire data is consumed by this method here (no-op returning 0).
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching readSetBegin().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolFactoryT::setStringSizeLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed string (and binary) size for protocols created by this factory. Enforced during reads.
requirements: string_limit should be non-negative (typical expectation for size limits; behavior for negatives is unspecified in this header).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolFactoryT::setContainerSizeLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed container size (lists, sets, maps) for protocols created by this factory. Enforced during reads.
requirements: container_limit should be non-negative (typical expectation for size limits; behavior for negatives is unspecified in this header).

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TCompactProtocolFactoryT::getProtocol
functions.description: Creates a Compact Protocol instance bound to the provided transport. If trans is compatible with the factory's Transport_ type, creates a TCompactProtocolT<Transport_>; otherwise creates a default TCompactProtocol. The created protocol is configured with any string/container limits set on the factory.
requirements: trans must be a non-null shared_ptr to a TTransport (or subclass).
Caller assumes ownership via the returned shared_ptr and must keep the underlying transport alive for the protocol's lifetime.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::TJSONProtocol
functions.description: Constructs a JSON protocol bound to the provided transport. Initializes internal context stack and a lookahead reader to parse/write JSON according to Thrift's JSON mapping. Typical usage: create with a transport (e.g., TMemoryBuffer or socket transport) and then call write*/read* APIs to serialize/deserialize.
requirements: ptrans must be a valid, non-null transport shared_ptr.
The transport must remain alive for the lifetime of the TJSONProtocol instance (the protocol stores a raw pointer to it internally).
The transport should be open/ready for I/O before performing read/write operations.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::~TJSONProtocol
functions.description: Destructor for the JSON protocol. Cleans up protocol resources; does not own or close the underlying transport.
requirements: The underlying transport is managed externally and is not closed by the destructor unless managed elsewhere.
No further operations should be performed on the protocol after destruction.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMessageBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMessageBegin(const std::string& name, const TMessageType messageType, const int32_t seqid)
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift message as a JSON array header containing protocol version, message name, message type, and sequence id.
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent call to writeMessageEnd().
name is the RPC method name and should be a valid UTF-8 string.
messageType must be a valid TMessageType enum value.
seqid should be the intended sequence identifier for matching requests/responses.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMessageEnd
functions.description: Ends a Thrift message started with writeMessageBegin(), closing any JSON constructs opened for the message.
requirements: Must be called after a successful writeMessageBegin().
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeStructBegin
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift struct as a JSON object. The name is unused for the wire format but may be used for debugging.
requirements: Must be paired with writeStructEnd().
name may be null or any C-string; it is not serialized on the wire.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeStructEnd
functions.description: Ends a Thrift struct previously started with writeStructBegin(), closing the JSON object representation.
requirements: Must be called after a matching writeStructBegin().
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeFieldBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeFieldBegin(const char* name, const TType fieldType, const int16_t fieldId)
functions.description: Begins writing a field inside a struct. Emits the field id as the JSON key and a type-tagged value envelope per Thrift JSON format.
requirements: Must be called between writeStructBegin() and writeStructEnd().
Must be followed by the field value writer (e.g., writeI32, writeString, writeStructBegin, etc.) and then writeFieldEnd().
fieldType must be a valid TType enum for the value being written.
fieldId should correspond to the field's declared id in the Thrift IDL.
name may be null or any C-string; it is not used by the wire format.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeFieldEnd
functions.description: Ends a field previously started with writeFieldBegin(), finalizing the JSON value envelope.
requirements: Must be called after a corresponding writeFieldBegin() and after writing the field's value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeFieldStop
functions.description: Signals the end of fields for a struct. With JSON protocol this may be a no-op but is part of the standard Thrift protocol API.
requirements: Should be called after all fields have been written and before writeStructEnd() if following standard Thrift patterns.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMapBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMapBegin(const TType keyType, const TType valType, const uint32_t size)
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift map as a JSON array header with key/value type identifiers and element count, followed by the key-value object.
requirements: Must be paired with writeMapEnd().
keyType and valType must be valid TType enums; JSON protocol requires map keys to be numeric or string types (non-binary).
size must be the number of key-value pairs that will be written.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeMapEnd
functions.description: Ends a Thrift map previously started with writeMapBegin(), closing the JSON constructs.
requirements: Must be called after a matching writeMapBegin() and after writing exactly the declared number of pairs.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeListBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeListBegin(const TType elemType, const uint32_t size)
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift list as a JSON array header with element type identifier and element count.
requirements: Must be paired with writeListEnd().
elemType must be a valid TType enum for all elements written.
size must equal the number of elements that will be written.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeListEnd
functions.description: Ends a Thrift list previously started with writeListBegin(), closing the JSON array.
requirements: Must be called after a matching writeListBegin() and after writing exactly the declared number of elements.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeSetBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeSetBegin(const TType elemType, const uint32_t size)
functions.description: Begins writing a Thrift set as a JSON array header with element type identifier and element count.
requirements: Must be paired with writeSetEnd().
elemType must be a valid TType enum for all elements written.
size must equal the number of elements that will be written.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeSetEnd
functions.description: Ends a Thrift set previously started with writeSetBegin(), closing the JSON array.
requirements: Must be called after a matching writeSetBegin() and after writing exactly the declared number of elements.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeBool
functions.description: Writes a Thrift boolean value, encoded under the current JSON context (typically within a field value).
requirements: Must be called in a valid context (e.g., after writeFieldBegin() or as a list/set/map element).
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeByte
functions.description: Writes a Thrift byte (i8) as a JSON number.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeI16
functions.description: Writes a Thrift i16 as a JSON number.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeI32
functions.description: Writes a Thrift i32 as a JSON number.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeI64
functions.description: Writes a Thrift i64 as a JSON number.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeDouble
functions.description: Writes a Thrift double as a JSON number, with special values possibly encoded as strings ("NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity").
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeString
functions.description: Writes a Thrift string as a JSON string with appropriate escaping.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Input must be valid byte data; content is escaped per JSON rules.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeBinary
functions.description: Writes a Thrift binary value as a Base64-encoded JSON string. Padding may be omitted per Thrift JSON specification.
requirements: Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Input is treated as raw bytes and will be Base64-encoded.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::writeUUID
functions.description: Writes a Thrift UUID value into its JSON representation according to the protocol's UUID handling.
requirements: uuid must be an initialized TUuid instance.
Must be called in a valid context for a value.
Transport must be writable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMessageBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMessageBegin(std::string& name, TMessageType& messageType, int32_t& seqid)
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift message from JSON, extracting the message name, type, and sequence id from the message header array.
requirements: Output parameters name, messageType, and seqid must be valid lvalue references.
Must be paired with readMessageEnd() when done reading the message body.
Transport must be readable and positioned at the start of a message.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMessageEnd
functions.description: Ends reading of a Thrift message previously started with readMessageBegin(), closing any remaining JSON constructs for the message.
requirements: Must follow a successful readMessageBegin().
Transport must be readable and positioned at the end of a message.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readStructBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift struct represented as a JSON object. The struct name is not carried on the wire; the returned name is typically unused.
requirements: name must be a valid lvalue reference (it may be set to an empty string).
Must be paired with readStructEnd().
Transport must be readable and positioned at a struct start.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readStructEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a Thrift struct previously started with readStructBegin(), closing the JSON object.
requirements: Must follow a matching readStructBegin().
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readFieldBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readFieldBegin(std::string& name, TType& fieldType, int16_t& fieldId)
functions.description: Begins reading a field within a struct. Extracts the field id (JSON key) and the type-tag for the upcoming value.
requirements: name, fieldType, and fieldId must be valid lvalue references for outputs.
Must be called between readStructBegin() and readStructEnd().
Must be followed by the appropriate read* for the field value and readFieldEnd().
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readFieldEnd
functions.description: Ends reading of a field started with readFieldBegin(), finalizing consumption of the field value envelope.
requirements: Must follow a corresponding readFieldBegin() and the value read.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMapBegin
functions.signature: uint32_t apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMapBegin(TType& keyType, TType& valType, uint32_t& size)
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift map encoded as a JSON array, returning key/value element types and the count of entries.
requirements: keyType, valType, and size must be valid lvalue references for outputs.
Must be paired with readMapEnd() after reading exactly size entries.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readMapEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a map previously started with readMapBegin(), closing the JSON constructs.
requirements: Must follow a matching readMapBegin() and after consuming the declared number of entries.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readListBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift list encoded as a JSON array, returning the element type and count.
requirements: elemType and size must be valid lvalue references for outputs.
Must be paired with readListEnd() after reading exactly size elements.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readListEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a list previously started with readListBegin(), closing the JSON array.
requirements: Must follow a matching readListBegin() and after consuming the declared number of elements.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readSetBegin
functions.description: Begins reading a Thrift set encoded as a JSON array, returning the element type and count.
requirements: elemType and size must be valid lvalue references for outputs.
Must be paired with readSetEnd() after reading exactly size elements.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readSetEnd
functions.description: Ends reading a set previously started with readSetBegin(), closing the JSON array.
requirements: Must follow a matching readSetBegin() and after consuming the declared number of elements.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readBool
functions.description: Reads a Thrift boolean value from JSON and stores it in value.
requirements: value must be a valid lvalue reference for output.
Must be called in a context expecting a boolean value.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readByte
functions.description: Reads a Thrift byte (i8) from JSON (as a number) and stores it in byte.
requirements: byte must be a valid lvalue reference for output.
Must be called in a context expecting an i8 value.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readI16
functions.description: Reads a Thrift i16 from JSON (as a number) and stores it.
requirements: i16 must be a valid lvalue reference for output.

Transport must be readable.

requirements: dub must be a valid lvalue reference for output.
Must be called in a context expecting a double value.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readString
functions.description: Reads a Thrift string from JSON, unescaping JSON string escapes.
requirements: str must be a valid lvalue reference for output.
Must be called in a context expecting a string value.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readBinary
functions.description: Reads a Thrift binary value from a Base64-encoded JSON string. Accepts input with or without Base64 padding.
requirements: str must be a valid lvalue reference for output.
Must be called in a context expecting a binary value; if called on a normal string, it will decode garbage data per the note in comments.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::readUUID
functions.description: Reads a Thrift UUID from its JSON representation into uuid.
requirements: uuid must be a valid lvalue reference to a TUuid to receive the parsed value.
Must be called in a context expecting a UUID value.
Transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::getMinSerializedSize
functions.description: Returns a lower-bound estimate of the minimum number of bytes required to serialize a value of the given Thrift type under this protocol. Used to pre-check available bytes before reading container payloads.
requirements: type must be a valid TType enum.
Return value is an estimate; actual JSON-encoded size may exceed this due to formatting and escaping.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::checkReadBytesAvailable
functions.description: Checks that the underlying transport has enough bytes available to read the elements of the given set, using getMinSerializedSize(elemType) * size as an estimate.
requirements: set.size_ and set.elemType_ must be correctly populated before calling.
Relies on getMinSerializedSize() which is a lower bound; JSON overhead may mean more bytes are actually needed.
Transport must support checkReadBytesAvailable().

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::LookaheadReader::LookaheadReader
functions.description: Constructs a lookahead reader helper around a transport. Allows peeking one byte ahead without consuming it, used by the JSON protocol parser.
requirements: trans must remain valid for the lifetime of the LookaheadReader instance.
The associated transport must be readable.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::LookaheadReader::read
functions.description: Reads and returns the next byte from the underlying transport. If a byte was previously peeked, it returns that and clears the peeked state.
requirements: Underlying transport must be readable.
May perform a blocking read depending on transport implementation.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocol::LookaheadReader::peek
functions.description: Peeks at the next byte from the underlying transport without consuming it. Subsequent read() will return the same byte.
requirements: Underlying transport must be readable.
May perform a blocking read depending on transport implementation.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocolFactory::TJSONProtocolFactory
functions.description: Default constructor for the JSON protocol factory. Produces TJSONProtocol instances on demand.
requirements: None beyond standard object construction.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocolFactory::~TJSONProtocolFactory
functions.description: Destructor for the JSON protocol factory.
requirements: None; does not own external resources beyond typical shared_ptr lifetimes.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TJSONProtocolFactory::getProtocol
functions.description: Creates and returns a new TJSONProtocol bound to the provided transport.
requirements: trans must be a valid, non-null transport shared_ptr ready for I/O.
The returned TProtocol shares ownership semantics with the provided transport via shared_ptr.

functions.name: apache::thrift::ThriftJSONString
functions.signature:
template <typename ThriftStruct>
std::string apache::thrift::ThriftJSONString(const ThriftStruct& ts)
functions.description: Utility template that serializes a Thrift struct to a JSON string using TMemoryBuffer and TJSONProtocol. It calls ts.write(&protocol) and returns the buffer contents as a std::string.
requirements: ThriftStruct must provide a write(TProtocol*) const method compatible with Thrift-generated structs.
ts must be a valid, initialized instance ready for serialization.
Sufficient memory must be available to hold the serialized JSON in a TMemoryBuffer.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolDecorator::~TProtocolDecorator
functions.description: Destructor for TProtocolDecorator. It performs default destruction and releases the reference to the wrapped TProtocol instance via shared_ptr.
requirements: No special requirements; safe to call when the object goes out of scope.
The underlying shared_ptr-managed TProtocol will be released when the last reference goes away.

functions.name: apache::thrift::protocol::TProtocolDecorator::TProtocolDecorator
functions.description: Constructs a TProtocolDecorator that forwards all protocol operations to the provided TProtocol. The decorator uses the underlying protocol's transport (via proto->getTransport()).
requirements: proto must point to a valid TProtocol instance (must not be null).
proto must remain valid for the lifetime of the decorator (managed via shared_ptr).
